lessons: Avoid starting with declarative background facts without an immediate tension or conflict, as seen in the Maple Syrup video where 38.5% of viewers dropped at 13% progress after a factual sap explanation.
Do not use explicit interactive pauses or calls to guess ('Pause and guess...'), as the Maple Syrup video suffered a 15.4% drop right at the 52% mark where this occurred.

Deliver a strong narrative or sensory hook immediately within the first 10% to push retention above 1.0 (rewatch territory); the Onions and Eyes videos achieved 1.178 and 1.065 at 10% respectively, whereas descriptive informational intros like Maple Syrup fell to 0.923.
Keep initial problem statements concise and direct; the Spicy Food video hook held reasonably well at the start (1.0479 at 10%), but generic setup lines caused high early friction across all samples.
worst_moment_types: Explanatory background trivia delivered without emotional or physical stakes
Direct prompt pauses asking the viewer to guess an answer
Slow informational tangents around the 13% to 26% video marks
best_hook_types: Intriguing sensory dilemmas or body mysteries (eyes leaking, onion crying, spicy food relief)
High-conflict physiological setups that defy expected intuition within the first few seconds
